answer: Each raven must be bound in the hollow, a public registry of manufacturer-certified enclave keys, to one delta, a physical secure chip whose key can back only one raven per 100 epochs. Ravens whose deltas report the same host, rack or IP block collide in the hollow, and the k-th raven in one rack needs k deltas. An honest raven buys one $200 chip. 1,000 co-located ravens need about 500,000 chips, or 1,000 chips spread across 1,000 real sites. It breaks if enclave keys are extracted or a vendor signs fake ones.
